review_kind: Independent assistant evidence review; not human risk annotation or calibrated ground truth
recommendation: HOLD / not accepted as a fully supported risk-change note

publication_scope.plan_scope: research only; stop at note gate; no publication

verdict_definitions.Supported: The narrow assertion is directly established by captured evidence or directly observed artifact scope/state. This is not a global eligibility/correctness certification.
verdict_definitions.Partial: The packet establishes part of a compound claim or requested condition; other retained parts are not demonstrated.
verdict_definitions.Unsupported: The retained assertion or acceptance inference has no supporting captured evidence, or is contradicted by the captured artifact. This does not imply the real-world proposition is false.
verdict_definitions.Unverified: The required comparative/provenance coverage is unavailable or incomplete, so no factual truth/falsehood decision is made.

claims.claim: Microsoft FY2024 discloses intellectual-property claims arising from AI training and output.
claims.assessment: The captured passage explicitly discusses current copyright/infringement claims arising from AI training/output and possible licensing, damages and operating-result consequences. This supports presence in FY2024, not novelty.
claims.gap: No gap for this narrow presence claim; source eligibility and complete-file provenance remain separate.
reviewer_steps: Retain a narrowly worded FY2024 presence statement with this passage.
Validate the original filing/version and source location under S05.

claims.claim: The Microsoft AI-IP risk was new or added in FY2024 relative to FY2023.
claims.assessment: The FY2023 captured opening concerns competition. Its silence on AI-IP does not establish absence elsewhere in the prior section. The handoff mentions prior IP passage _071, but its full text is not in the final cited packet.
claims.gap: Comparable FY2023 IP/AI coverage, exclusions and relocation/cross-reference checks are missing.
reviewer_steps: Recover the authentic historical FY2023 IP topic and relevant cross-references.
Compare equivalent coverage with FY2024 _081; record absence only within a demonstrated reviewed scope.
Until then replace new/added with present in FY2024 and state that change cannot be classified.

claims.claim: Microsoft FY2024 discusses climate-related resource, energy, powering and cooling costs.
claims.assessment: The captured text explicitly identifies uncertain long-term climate effects, resource/energy availability or cost and increased powering/cooling costs.
claims.gap: No gap for the narrow FY2024 disclosure-presence statement.
reviewer_steps: Keep a conditional statement matching the passage, without claiming realised cost effects or newness.

claims.claim: Microsoft climate disclosure was expanded or newly added in FY2024 versus FY2023.
claims.assessment: The captured FY2023 competition opening is not the comparable climate disclosure. The FY2024 passage supports current content only.
claims.gap: Prior climate/topic coverage and actual paired wording are absent from the final cited packet.
reviewer_steps: Retrieve and verify the prior climate/environmental topic and cross-references.
Record whether the difference is substantive content, wording or relocation.
Use an insufficient-comparable-evidence limitation until that comparison is complete.

claims.claim: Microsoft competition, IP, source-code and pandemic risks were updated with broader results-of-operations language.
claims.assessment: The packet establishes FY2023 competition text and FY2024 IP/source-code and pandemic-tail content. It does not contain corresponding before-and-after text for every retained topic. Different topics cannot demonstrate a paired wording update.
claims.gap: Missing captured counterparts: FY2024 competition and FY2023 IP/source-code/pandemic. Handoff IDs alone are not full evidence.
reviewer_steps: Break this bundled sentence into separate topic-level assertions.
Resolve the handoff passage IDs to complete authentic text and pair like topics.
Keep only differences actually supported by reviewed pairs.

claims.claim: Alphabet FY2024 describes manufacturing/supply-chain reliance on contract manufacturers and other third parties.
claims.assessment: The captured passage directly describes devices, servers/networking equipment, components, distribution and third-party capacity/obligation/pricing risks.
claims.gap: No gap for FY2024 presence; the trailing Table of Contents footer does not negate the substantive risk text.
reviewer_steps: Retain the narrowly supported FY2024 description and conditional wording.

claims.claim: Alphabet introduced a new manufacturing and supply-chain risk in FY2024.
claims.assessment: The FY2023 opening is an advertising-risk paragraph. It cannot establish that manufacturing/supply-chain text was absent elsewhere in FY2023.
claims.gap: Comparable prior manufacturing/supply-chain coverage and absence/relocation review are not captured.
reviewer_steps: Review the earlier complete topic/section and related cross-references from the historical source snapshot.
Classify newness only after adequate paired coverage.
Otherwise remove new/added/introduced and preserve presence plus a comparison limitation.

claims.claim: Alphabet advertising, device-access, privacy/security and operating-result-fluctuation risks remained consistent with minor wording changes.
claims.assessment: The captured prior passage supports advertising-risk presence; the captured current passage concerns a different supply-chain topic. Neither supplies the complete paired evidence for the four-topic continuity claim. The handoff names extra IDs, whose full texts are not captured here.
claims.gap: Actual matched-year passages and reviewed coverage for all four topics are missing from the final cited packet.
reviewer_steps: Recover the handoff pairs and verify them before retaining any continuity statement.
Limit Unchanged to the reviewed topic/scope, not the whole Item 1A section.

claims.claim: Microsoft new AI-IP risk aligns with an increased company focus on AI technologies.
claims.assessment: The risk paragraph establishes AI-related claims, not a measured increase in strategic focus. No supporting strategy/time-comparison evidence is attached to this sentence in the captured packet. Unsupported here means not supported by this evidence packet, not proved false.
claims.gap: Evidence for the increased-focus comparison and its periods is missing; newness also depends on R02.
reviewer_steps: Remove the strategic-focus inference or add a directly supporting, attributed management source and explicit comparison.
Do not use this sentence to imply a financial cause.

claims.claim: No direct causal linkage between risk-disclosure changes and margin movements is established in the available filings.
claims.assessment: This is an appropriate caution: the captured risk passages do not establish a causal margin explanation. However, no exhaustive review of the available filings is recorded, and risk-change existence is itself unverified.
claims.gap: The scope of the negative finding is broader than the demonstrated reviewed evidence. This limitation does not cure R02/R04/R07.
reviewer_steps: Use: No direct causal linkage is established by the passages reviewed for this note.
Separately state whether each disclosure change can be classified; do not substitute lack of causation for missing prior coverage.

claims.claim: The response accounts for both requested companies and all three financial years.
claims.assessment: The draft explicitly lists MSFT and Alphabet margins for FY2022, FY2023 and FY2024. The six displayed percentages match the supplied reference values, but this scope observation is not independent financial/source-eligibility verification.
claims.gap: Financial concepts, inputs, formulas and source eligibility require the separate financial review.
reviewer_steps: Cross-reference the financial reviewer's source and calculation checks; do not promote this presence check to full verification.

claims.claim: The note covers risk disclosures in the FY2022–FY2024 years retained by the approved plan.
claims.assessment: The approved plan asks about risks in these years, and explicitly retains FY2022/2023/2024. Both risk handoffs compare 2024 with 2023. No FY2022 Item 1A is in the final cited packet; no explicit scope change or coverage limitation accounts for that year. Replans is zero.
claims.gap: FY2022 risk evidence and any requested 2022-to-2023 or 2022-to-2024 transition are unaccounted for. The original request does not by itself choose every possible pair, so the intended pair set must be clarified rather than assumed.
reviewer_steps: R1 confirms the intended pair set under the approved all-years question.
R3 preserves every agreed company/year/pair in the research plan and output.
R2 supplies the missing source coverage or an explicit insufficient-evidence result; any narrowed task needs an explicit revised-scope decision.

claims.claim: Actual fiscal-period differences requested in the approved plan are disclosed.
claims.assessment: Only FY2022 period ends (June 30 and December 31) are explicit in the draft. FY2023/FY2024 actual starts and ends and a direct explanation of unequal reporting windows are absent. No new-code Comparability section appears in this historical artifact.
claims.gap: The later-year reporting windows and cross-company comparability caveat are not fully stated.
reviewer_steps: After financial source review, state the actual requested-year periods and explain that each company's own FY differs from a common calendar window.
Do not credit comparability code added at 33fef7f as observed behaviour of this 42e2298 note.

claims.claim: The draft states insufficient evidence where risk changes cannot be established.
claims.assessment: The limitations discuss absent causal links, but continue to call AI, climate and supply-chain disclosures new/expanded/added. They do not say that earlier-year comparable coverage is insufficient to classify these changes. This is an observable missing acceptance condition, not proof the real-world risks were old or new.
claims.gap: A topic-specific unverified-change limitation is missing for R02/R04/R07 and the bundled continuity/update assertions.
reviewer_steps: Replace unsupported change labels or complete the paired evidence review.
Display the affected company/topic/pair and the precise missing coverage instead of a generic causal disclaimer.

Resolve original-document URLs and filing dates/version eligibility as needed, preserving the historical revision.

claims.claim: The captured baseline item1a_000 passages are table-of-contents-only extracts.
claims.assessment: Both captured baseline passages contain substantive risk-section opening prose: Microsoft strategic/competitive risk and Alphabet advertising risk. MSFT's initial heading is clipped to K FACTORS, but it is not TOC-only. Alphabet FY2024 _020 has a trailing Table of Contents footer plus real supply-chain prose.

reviewer_steps: Describe the actual captured text accurately.
Do not treat an opening passage or incidental footer as proof of complete section coverage.

claims.claim: This review may treat the saved plan approval as note/publication approval.
claims.assessment: The captured plan approval explicitly limits scope to research, stopping at the note gate with no publication. The result is waiting_note, next review_note, check.ok=false, revisions=2. No final-note approval, published outcome or publication receipt is present in these artifacts.
claims.gap: The note is not an accepted/published result in the captured state. No live portal was queried, so this is not a global proof that no portal record exists.
reviewer_steps: Keep the review and note on HOLD; make no approval or publication action.
Any future acceptance requires completed checks, resolved scope/evidence issues and a fresh explicit decision for the exact eligible note.
Preserve the historical failed/incomplete state even if a later version succeeds.
